cards.title: Problem
cards.question: What type of problem or need must justify the project, and where must it originate?
cards.answer:
The need is an industrial company's: reducing its CO2 emissions in the Netherlands, where a pilot, demonstration or proven-technology investment needs a study before the company can decide to invest.
Industry means companies that make tangible goods, process raw materials and work with a high degree of mechanisation and automation, in practice those in the Dutch standard business classification (SBI) groups B (mining), C (manufacturing), D (only energy distribution and gas production) or E (water, waste and remediation); RVO decides at assessment whether an activity counts as industry. One of the applicants must be able to use the study results in its own company and must intend to invest in the follow-up project. The call addresses topics such as electrification, energy efficiency, secondary raw materials, CO2 capture and other CO2-reducing measures.
cards.sources:
Staatscourant 2026, 15135 · Bijlage A (bijlage 4.2.16), § 1 Doel

cards.title: Deliverables
cards.question: Which concrete outputs must the project produce?
cards.answer:
A study report that supports an investment decision, plus a final report on business case, market factors and scale-up.
With the request for final settlement, the recipient must deliver:
- a final report covering the financial or economic opportunities, including one or more business models; the non-technological factors for market application and how they are handled; and the scale-up and replication potential;
- a report on the next steps the consortium will take to implement what was studied, and the expected CO2 reduction if it is implemented.
cards.sources: Regeling nationale EZ-, LVVN- en KGG-subsidies (wetten.overheid.nl, version 6 May 2026) · § 4.2.17 · Artikel 4.2.117a, tweede lid; Artikel 4.2.118 Aanvraag subsidievaststelling

cards.title: Impact
cards.question: Which wider system outcomes and impacts must the project support?
cards.answer:
The follow-up project must reduce CO2 emissions in Dutch industrial processes cost-effectively within ten years after the study ends.
CO2 reduction also includes avoiding future emissions from new factories with activities new to the Netherlands, compared with a conventional reference investment that meets Dutch minimum environmental standards; capturing atmospheric or biogenic CO2 for use or storage; producing green gas by gasification and sustainable transport fuels; and producing and importing renewable hydrogen for industry and mobility. The call sets no numeric targets, but the final report must state the expected CO2 reduction.
cards.sources:
Staatscourant 2026, 15135 · Bijlage A (bijlage 4.2.16), § 1 Doel
Regeling nationale EZ-, LVVN- en KGG-subsidies (wetten.overheid.nl, version 6 May 2026) · § 4.2.17 · Artikel 4.2.117a, tweede lid, onderdeel b

cards.title: After the project
cards.question: How must the result be replicated, taken up and kept in use after the project?
cards.answer:
The study must lead credibly to a follow-up investment by an industrial company and its results must be shared.
- The company must intend to invest in the follow-up project; the project plan must describe the next steps towards implementation if the result is positive, or the application is rejected.
- The applicant must provide for good-quality knowledge dissemination.
- The final report must cover scale-up and replication potential and the business models needed for market application.
The call does not require the follow-up project actually to be carried out.
cards.sources:
Regeling nationale EZ-, LVVN- en KGG-subsidies (wetten.overheid.nl, version 6 May 2026) · § 4.2.17 · Artikel 4.2.113; Artikel 4.2.117, onderdelen b en d; Artikel 4.2.118

cards.title: Number of partners
cards.question: What is the permitted or required consortium size?
cards.answer: A single company may apply alone, or a consortium (samenwerkingsverband) may apply; a consortium needs at least one company with an interest in the results that intends to invest. No maximum is set.
cards.sources:
Regeling nationale EZ-, LVVN- en KGG-subsidies (wetten.overheid.nl, version 6 May 2026) · § 4.2.17 · Artikel 4.2.113, onderdelen a en b
STUDI: Studies voor duurzame industrie (RVO page) · Extra voorwaarden voor een samenwerkingsverband

cards.title: Partner composition
cards.question: Which types of partners must the consortium include?
cards.answer:
At least one company that takes part, has an interest in the results and plans to invest in the follow-up project; research organisations, other companies and local governments may join.
- Municipalities and provinces may take part but receive no subsidy.
- If a research organisation takes part, a signed collaboration agreement is needed before the study starts.
- No company in the consortium may be a company in difficulty under EU state aid rules, unless it applies for de-minimis aid instead.
- The call sets no country rule for partners; the follow-up project must reduce emissions in Dutch industry.
cards.sources:
STUDI: Studies voor duurzame industrie (RVO page) · Voor wie?; Extra voorwaarden voor een samenwerkingsverband
Regeling nationale EZ-, LVVN- en KGG-subsidies (wetten.overheid.nl, version 6 May 2026) · § 4.2.17 · Artikel 4.2.113

cards.title: Distribution of work
cards.question: How must work and budget be distributed among partners?
cards.answer:
The consortium must be sufficiently balanced, shown by how costs are split between participants or by the ratio of private to public funding; otherwise the application is rejected.
- Costs of a company in the applicant's own group with a Dutch establishment are subsidised up to EUR 25,000; above that, that company must itself be a participant.
- For an environmental or comparable study on proven technology, only costs of activities by third parties outside the consortium and the group count.
cards.sources:
Regeling nationale EZ-, LVVN- en KGG-subsidies (wetten.overheid.nl, version 6 May 2026) · § 4.2.17 · Artikel 4.2.114, zevende lid; Artikel 4.2.114a, vierde lid; Artikel 4.2.117, onderdeel c

cards.title: Coordinator
cards.question: What type of organisation may or must act as lead applicant?
cards.answer:
A company that carries out the study itself, or any participant in a consortium that includes at least one company, may apply.
The study must serve a possible follow-up investment by that company, or by a company in its group, and one of the applying companies must be able to use the results in its own business.
cards.sources:
Regeling nationale EZ-, LVVN- en KGG-subsidies (wetten.overheid.nl, version 6 May 2026) · § 4.2.17 · Artikel 4.2.113

project_requirements.title: TenneT's position
project_requirements.question: What is TenneT's position within the consortium?

cards.title: Coordinate
cards.question: Can TenneT apply or coordinate, and under which conditions?
cards.answer:
Probably not as sole applicant, because the study must prepare an investment by a company in industry; TenneT could apply on behalf of a consortium only if it includes such a company.
Under the rules, the subsidy goes to a company carrying out the study for its own follow-up investment, or to a participant in a consortium. TenneT TSO B.V. transmits electricity, which is not one of the industry groups RVO names (SBI group D counts only for energy distribution and gas production), and RVO decides what counts as industry. In a consortium with an industrial company that plans to invest, TenneT could in principle submit the application, but the industrial partner is the natural lead.
cards.sources:
Regeling nationale EZ-, LVVN- en KGG-subsidies (wetten.overheid.nl, version 6 May 2026) · § 4.2.17 · Artikel 4.2.113
Staatscourant 2026, 15135 · Bijlage A (bijlage 4.2.16), § 1 Doel (definition of industry)
STUDI: Studies voor duurzame industrie (RVO page) · Voorwaarden

cards.title: Participate
cards.question: Can TenneT take part without receiving funding?
cards.answer:
Yes. TenneT can be a participant in a consortium led by an industrial company, with or without requesting subsidy for its own costs.
The rules only require at least one company that intends to invest; other participants are allowed. Only municipalities and provinces are excluded from receiving subsidy. TenneT could therefore also take part without requesting a grant, but the consortium must stay balanced.
cards.sources:
Regeling nationale EZ-, LVVN- en KGG-subsidies (wetten.overheid.nl, version 6 May 2026) · § 4.2.17 · Artikel 4.2.113, onderdeel b; Artikel 4.2.117, onderdeel c
STUDI: Studies voor duurzame industrie (RVO page) · Voor wie?

cards.title: Receive funding
cards.question: Can TenneT receive funding, and which funding rate or cost rules apply?
cards.answer:
Yes, in our interpretation: each participant in a consortium can receive subsidy, so TenneT TSO B.V. could receive 50% of its eligible study costs as a large company.
- Funding rate: 50% for a large company or research organisation (60% for a medium-sized, 70% for a small company).
- Eligible costs: for a feasibility study the costs of the study under EU research aid rules; for an environmental study the costs under EU environmental aid rules; for a comparable study the costs of the study.
- Cap: EUR 4 million per feasibility or environmental study and per follow-up project per round; EUR 300,000 per participant over three years for a comparable study.
TenneT must therefore pay at least half of its own study costs itself.
cards.sources:
Regeling nationale EZ-, LVVN- en KGG-subsidies (wetten.overheid.nl, version 6 May 2026) · § 4.2.17 · Artikel 4.2.113, onderdeel b; Artikel 4.2.114; Artikel 4.2.114a
STUDI: Studies voor duurzame industrie (RVO page) · Hoeveel subsidie krijgt u?

cards.title: TenneT's likely contribution
cards.question: What contribution would make TenneT credible and useful within the project?
cards.answer: Our judgement: TenneT would be most useful as a partner in a study by an industrial company or cluster that plans to electrify, contributing the grid side: connection options and timing, available transmission capacity, flexible or time-dependent connection contracts and grid-reinforcement needs, which often decide whether an electrification investment is feasible. This fits TenneT's work in the Energy boards and its Grid Investment Plans, and the call's focus on preparing an investment decision makes realistic grid input valuable to the industrial partner. TenneT should keep its own costs in proportion to its role, since the consortium must be balanced and the follow-up investment must be made by an industrial company.
cards.sources:
STUDI: Studies voor duurzame industrie (RVO page) · Waarvoor krijgt u subsidie?; Extra voorwaarden voor een samenwerkingsverband

project_requirements.title: Innovation
project_requirements.question: What type of innovation must the project develop?

cards.title: Innovation threshold
cards.question: Must the project produce genuinely new knowledge or technology, or may it integrate and apply existing solutions?
cards.answer:
The study itself need not produce new technology, but a pilot or demonstration project it prepares must use sufficiently innovative technology.
- For a pilot or demonstration project, the application is rejected if the technique is not innovative enough; a demonstration project must be new to the Netherlands or apply technology in a way new to the Netherlands.
- For a proven-technology project, the technology need not be new, but the payback time of the investment must be more than five years.
cards.sources:
Regeling nationale EZ-, LVVN- en KGG-subsidies (wetten.overheid.nl, version 6 May 2026) · § 4.2.17 · Artikel 4.2.112 (demonstratieproject, project met uitontwikkelde technologie); Artikel 4.2.117, onderdeel i
STUDI: Studies voor duurzame industrie (RVO page) · Wanneer wijzen wij uw aanvraag af?

cards.title: Innovation object
cards.question: In what must the project innovate?
cards.answer: The call funds studies on technology and investment, not market or governance innovation: the object is an industrial installation or process that reduces CO2, together with its business case, permits and legal set-up.
cards.sources:
Staatscourant 2026, 15135 · Bijlage A (bijlage 4.2.16), § 1 Doel
STUDI: Studies voor duurzame industrie (RVO page) · Waarvoor krijgt u subsidie?

cards.title: Development stages
cards.question: Which development stages must the project cover?
cards.answer:
Only the study stage that comes before a pilot, demonstration or proven-technology investment; research, development and construction are excluded.
- Feasibility study: before a pilot project.
- Environmental study: before a demonstration project or proven-technology investment.
- Comparable study: before a demonstration project or proven-technology investment.
cards.sources:
Staatscourant 2026, 15135 · Bijlage A (bijlage 4.2.16), § 1 Doel (table)
Regeling nationale EZ-, LVVN- en KGG-subsidies (wetten.overheid.nl, version 6 May 2026) · § 4.2.17 · Artikel 4.2.112

cards.title: Maturity
cards.question: Which maturity level is expected at the start and end of the project?
cards.answer: The call names no TRL (technology readiness level). The follow-up project ranges from a pilot, where a prototype is tested in a realistic setting, to technology already proven in one or more demonstration projects.
cards.sources: Regeling nationale EZ-, LVVN- en KGG-subsidies (wetten.overheid.nl, version 6 May 2026) · § 4.2.17 · Artikel 4.2.112 Begripsbepalingen

project_requirements.title: Work
project_requirements.question: Which activities or work structure must the project cover?

cards.title: Demonstration
cards.question: Where and under which conditions must the solution be demonstrated?
cards.answer: No demonstration is funded: the study prepares a later pilot or demonstration; only limited test work, such as testing samples, is allowed.
cards.sources:
STUDI: Studies voor duurzame industrie (RVO page) · Voorwaarden
Regeling nationale EZ-, LVVN- en KGG-subsidies (wetten.overheid.nl, version 6 May 2026) · § 4.2.17 · Artikel 4.2.117, onderdeel h

cards.title: Integration
cards.question: How must the activities fit together and with existing systems?
cards.answer:
The study must be about a concrete industrial project and must be usable in the applying company's own business.
The results must feed an investment decision on that project, and the project plan must describe the steps to implementation. For hydrogen import facilities, the follow-up must fit the EU definitions of energy infrastructure or specific infrastructure.
cards.sources:
Regeling nationale EZ-, LVVN- en KGG-subsidies (wetten.overheid.nl, version 6 May 2026) · § 4.2.17 · Artikel 4.2.113; Artikel 4.2.117, onderdeel d

cards.title: Evidence
cards.question: What must the demonstration prove?
cards.answer: The final report must show the financial and economic opportunities, non-technological factors, scale-up potential and the expected CO2 reduction; for CO2 capture studies in programme line 1, also detailed cost and installation data.
cards.sources: Regeling nationale EZ-, LVVN- en KGG-subsidies (wetten.overheid.nl, version 6 May 2026) · § 4.2.17 · Artikel 4.2.117a, tweede lid; Artikel 4.2.118

cards.title: User participation
cards.question: How must users take part in the project?
cards.answer: The company that will use the results and invest must itself take part in the study.

cards.question: Which safety, cybersecurity or data requirements must the project meet?

funding_timing_submission.title: Funding
funding_timing_submission.question: How much funding can the project receive?

cards.title: Funding envelope
cards.answer:
A budget of EUR 28.3 million, allocated first come, first served, with at most EUR 4 million subsidy per feasibility or environmental study.
- Total project size: not limited; at 50% for a large company, the EUR 4 million cap corresponds to EUR 8 million of eligible costs.
- Grant request: up to EUR 4 million per feasibility or environmental study, and in total per follow-up project per round; up to EUR 300,000 per company or per consortium participant over three years for a comparable study; at least EUR 25,000 for an environmental or comparable study on proven technology; at most EUR 300,000 over three years for a company in difficulty.
- Funding form: a project subsidy on actual eligible costs.
The budget is oversubscribed: on 16 October 2026 nothing was left, but applications are still accepted because budget can come free when applications are rejected.
cards.sources:
Regeling nationale EZ-, LVVN- en KGG-subsidies (wetten.overheid.nl, version 6 May 2026) · § 4.2.17 · Artikel 4.2.114, vierde tot en met zesde lid; Artikel 4.2.115; Artikel 4.2.117, onderdeel g
Staatscourant 2026, 15135 · Artikel II, onderdeel B
STUDI: Studies voor duurzame industrie (RVO page) · Budget en aanvraagperiode

cards.title: Funding rate and co-financing
cards.answer:
The subsidy is 50% of eligible costs, raised by 10 percentage points for medium-sized and 20 for small companies that incur and pay the costs themselves.
- Large company or research organisation: 50%
- Medium-sized company: 60%
- Small company: 70%
- Co-financing conditions: the participants pay the rest themselves; the consortium must be balanced in its split of costs or in its private and public funding.
- Evidence required: an SME declaration for small and medium-sized companies; an explanation of the own contribution; a de-minimis declaration for comparable studies.
cards.sources:
Regeling nationale EZ-, LVVN- en KGG-subsidies (wetten.overheid.nl, version 6 May 2026) · § 4.2.17 · Artikel 4.2.114, eerste tot en met derde lid; Artikel 4.2.117, onderdeel c

cards.title: Budget constraints
cards.answer:
Only costs directly linked to the study count, with limits on group-company costs and on test work.
- Eligible costs: personnel and other costs directly connected with carrying out the study, supported by quotes where possible.
- Caps or mandatory allocations: at most EUR 25,000 subsidy for costs of a group company with a Dutch establishment that is not itself a participant; test work may be at most half of the costs.
- Excluded costs: for an environmental or comparable study on proven technology, costs within the consortium or the applicant's group.
cards.sources:

funding_timing_submission.title: Timing
funding_timing_submission.question: What timing should the proposal submission and project follow?

cards.title: Application route
cards.answer:
One stage: online through RVO with eHerkenning level 3, from 18 May 2026, 09:00, to 31 March 2027, 17:00, first come, first served.
- Stage 1 — Application: by 31 March 2027, 17:00 (the opening table in Staatscourant 2026, 15135 prints the end date as 31-03-2026, which appears to be a typing error; RVO states 31 March 2027). Filling in takes about 1.5 hours.
- Additional procedure: RVO offers an optional check of the project idea through a project idea form before applying.
cards.sources:

Staatscourant 2026, 15135 · Artikel II, onderdeel B

cards.title: Project window
cards.answer:
A study lasts at most one year for a subsidy up to EUR 1 million and at most two years above that.
- Maximum duration: 12 months (subsidy up to EUR 1 million) or 24 months (more than EUR 1 million).
- Required start: with a research organisation in the consortium, not before the collaboration agreement is signed.
cards.sources:
Regeling nationale EZ-, LVVN- en KGG-subsidies (wetten.overheid.nl, version 6 May 2026) · § 4.2.17 · Artikel 4.2.116 Realisatietermijn

cards.title: Decision and contracting
cards.answer:
RVO assesses applications in order of receipt and sends a decision; after a grant, the recipient reports progress, reports changes and applies for final settlement.
- Conditions before starting: a signed collaboration agreement when a research organisation takes part.
cards.sources:

funding_timing_submission.title: Application
funding_timing_submission.question: Mandatory information to include in the application

cards.title: Mandatory submission package — pass/fail
cards.answer:
An online application with the required annexes, a cost budget and statements on state aid.
- Application form: online in Mijn RVO; save in between.
- Budget: the costs per activity, supported by quotes.
- Mandatory annexes: a project plan that describes the approach, risks, feasibility, participants and the steps after the study; an explanation of the own contribution.
- Partner documents: an SME declaration where applicable; a statement that no company is in difficulty, with the decision scheme provided by the minister; a de-minimis declaration for comparable studies or companies in difficulty.
- Registration: eHerkenning level 3 with authorisation for RVO services at eH3.
cards.sources:
STUDI: Aanvragen (RVO page) · Uw aanvraag voorbereiden

cards.title: Evaluation and selection — scored or ranked
cards.answer:
Applications are not ranked: complete applications are granted in order of receipt, unless a rejection ground applies.
- Evaluation criteria: rejection if the quality is insufficient (approach and method, handling of risks, feasibility, participants, effective and efficient use of money), if knowledge dissemination is insufficient, if the consortium is unbalanced, or if the next steps after the study are not described well enough.
- Ranking rules: first come, first served.
cards.sources:
Regeling nationale EZ-, LVVN- en KGG-subsidies (wetten.overheid.nl, version 6 May 2026) · § 4.2.17 · Artikel 4.2.115; Artikel 4.2.117

cards.title: Conditional and exceptional requirements
cards.answer:
Extra rules apply to particular study types and companies.
- Exception — comparable study: funded as de-minimis aid, up to EUR 300,000 per company over three years, with a de-minimis declaration; not open to fisheries, aquaculture or primary agriculture.
- Exception — company in difficulty: may only receive de-minimis aid, up to EUR 300,000 over three years.
- Conditional — proven technology: payback time must plausibly exceed five years, and the subsidy must be at least EUR 25,000.
- Recommended: preparing for an EU Innovation Fund application can be eligible; RVO asks applicants to submit a project idea form first.
